questions.prompt: A single-raised pot is not a limped pot because…

choices.text: Someone showed a stronger range by raising.

questions.explanation: Use the raiser’s range, not a limp range, when you put them on hands.

choices.text: Small, in position, dry ace-high, as the raiser.
A donk with bottom pair into the raiser

questions.explanation: Small on dry high boards. Not the other three.

questions.prompt: The caller should lead most often when…

choices.text: The flop hits the calling range much harder than the opening range.
They are in position and can check back

questions.explanation: Leads are the exception inside single-raised pots.

questions.prompt: If the flop checks through, the turn plan…

choices.text: Starts fresh. Either player can bet a card that helps them.
Is over. The hand checks down
Belongs only to the big blind

questions.explanation: A checked flop is a delayed-bet spot, not a surrender.
